label: Cisco Systems 2000 — telecom infrastructure overbuild
episode: Dot-com fiber/networking buildout unwind
outcome_summary: Stock fell -89% from peak ($80 to $8.60). Revenue declined from $8.9B to $4.4B annualized. $2.25B inventory write-down in Q3 2001. Installed base extended replacement cycles, suppressing demand. Stock never returned to 2000 peak.
why_relevant: The bull thesis for any infrastructure supplier whose revenue depends on customer capex rests on the same structural claim: customers must spend this capex to remain competitive. Cisco's customers believed the same in 1999. When the capital cycle turns, there are no purchase orders to cancel because there are no purchase orders to place. The mechanism is identical for any infrastructure supplier at peak-multiple facing a customer capex cycle inflection.
disanalogy: AI capex is funded from $100B+ FCF balance sheets, not debt-financed startup capital — the quality of demand is structurally different. The AI infrastructure thesis has a real end-demand revenue signal (model-serving revenue) vs. telecom, which projected internet traffic growth that never monetized at assumed levels. GPU upgrade cycles are shorter than networking equipment (CUDA generations compress refresh cycles), limiting installed-base suppression. Concentration is lower: NVDA sells to four hyperscalers, not one AT&T.
base_rate_note: Infrastructure suppliers typically recover operationally within 3-5 years. The Cisco stock price never recovered because the 2000 valuation embedded permanent premium growth that was never realized — the operational business survived but the multiple paid was permanently wrong.
source_note: Cisco 10-K filings 2000-2002; Federal Reserve H.15; Bloomberg

label: NVIDIA 2022 — gaming GPU channel inventory correction
episode: Post-crypto/COVID GPU demand normalization
outcome_summary: Stock fell -69% from peak ($346 to $108). Gaming revenue guidance cut -33% in August 2022. Channel held 6-9 months excess GPU inventory from crypto/COVID demand. Data center remained strong but could not offset gaming collapse. Revenue normalized over 3-4 quarters; stock recovered to new all-time highs within 18 months as AI replaced gaming as growth driver.
why_relevant: For any semiconductor company where a portion of demand was supply-constrained and customers were building safety stock, the post-constraint normalization almost always results in a channel correction. The distinction between channels emptying and underlying demand collapsing is exactly what was missed in 2022. The data center mix was not affected — illustrating that segment diversification is the key variable in severity.
disanalogy: Data center demand for NVDA in 2024+ purchases direct from hyperscalers — no channel inventory builds. The 2022 correction was amplified by a 425bps rate rise that compressed a 60x+ multiple; that multiple compression cannot repeat at normalized valuations. Crypto GPU demand is no longer part of the NVDA bull thesis; the question is AI data center, a different and better-supported use case.
base_rate_note: Semiconductor channel corrections typically resolve in 2-6 quarters. The NVDA 2022 correction resolved within 3 quarters because data center growth absorbed the revenue mix shift — an unusually fast resolution driven by the AI demand acceleration.

label: Micron 2022-2023 — semiconductor memory inventory supercycle trough
episode: Post-COVID DRAM/NAND demand collapse
outcome_summary: Revenue fell from $8.7B/qtr to $3.7B/qtr (-57%) in two quarters. Gross margins went negative (-31.4% in Q2 FY2023). Company aggressively cut capex and production. Customers had 6-12 months of DRAM/NAND buffer inventory. Revenue recovered within 4-5 quarters as inventory normalized.
why_relevant: Memory is the purest semiconductor cycle instrument — the inventory correction mechanism is cleaner and more extreme here than anywhere else in semiconductors, making it the strongest calibration anchor for severity expectations in analogous category corrections. The -57% revenue decline in two quarters illustrates the maximum velocity of the channel correction mechanism.
disanalogy: AI workloads have structurally higher HBM (high-bandwidth memory) intensity than prior compute cycles, providing a demand floor that did not exist in the 2022 correction. Micron's supply discipline (faster capex cuts than prior cycles due to experience) shortened this correction relative to prior memory cycles. The memory cycle always overshoots in both directions; amplitude varies by cycle.
base_rate_note: Memory is the most cyclical semiconductor category; corrections of 40-60% revenue magnitude occur approximately every 3-5 years. Gross margins reliably return to mid-cycle norms as inventory normalizes — the business model is not permanently impaired by the correction.

label: Texas Instruments 2022-2023 — analog/embedded channel inventory correction
episode: Industrial and automotive chip inventory normalization
outcome_summary: Revenue declined from $5.1B/qtr to $3.8B/qtr (-25%) over five quarters. Gross margins compressed ~800bps from peak. No crypto or AI demand noise — pure industrial/automotive channel correction. Recovery slower than memory because automotive/industrial design cycles are longer. Broadest observable pure-play channel correction in semiconductors.
why_relevant: TI's correction is the cleanest pure-play channel inventory signal in semiconductors — no crypto, no AI noise, no rate-shock amplification. It isolates the mechanism with almost no confounding factors, making it the best calibration anchor for industrial semiconductor inventory correction duration and amplitude.
disanalogy: TI explicitly builds inventory as a strategic competitive advantage (300mm fabs moat) — the correction was partially a deliberate industry behavior change unique to TI's strategy. Automotive electrification content per vehicle is growing secularly, providing a demand floor that moderates future cycle amplitude. The -25% severity was shallower than consumer or memory corrections.
base_rate_note: Industrial semiconductor corrections are typically shallower but longer-duration than consumer or memory corrections because customer inventory positions change more slowly and design-in cycles are longer.

label: NVIDIA 2018 — crypto mining demand air pocket
episode: Crypto bear market GPU demand collapse
outcome_summary: Revenue guidance cut twice in three months: from $3.4B to $2.7B to $2.2B. Peak $293 to trough $124, -57% in 60 days. Crypto mining GPU demand ($1.3B annualized at peak) evaporated in weeks when BTC fell from $19,500 to $3,200. Gaming underlying demand was never impaired — only the speculative use case disappeared. Recovered within 12 months.
why_relevant: When demand is tied to speculative activity rather than productive use, it does not normalize — it disappears. This is the critical distinction from channel correction. Any thesis that assigns durable demand to speculative or pull-forward use cases deserves the air-pocket frame. The guidance credibility damage (cut twice in three months) is a recurring outcome of over-relying on speculative demand.
disanalogy: AI/data center demand in 2024+ is explicitly productive (revenue-generating model serving); it is not speculative like crypto mining. NVDA explicitly learned from 2018 — they now require sell-through data and do not plan inventory for speculative use cases. The 2018 event was small relative to total revenue (crypto was <15%) compared to current AI data center concentration — the direction of risk has reversed.
base_rate_note: Demand air pockets tied to speculative use cases are typically faster and sharper than channel corrections but also recover more cleanly because the underlying productive demand (gaming) was never impaired. Duration: weeks to months vs. quarters for channel corrections.

label: Zoom Video 2022 — pandemic pull-forward demand air pocket
episode: Post-pandemic re-opening demand normalization
outcome_summary: Revenue growth went from 326% YoY to -4% over two years. Peak $568 (October 2020) to trough $57 (December 2022), -90%. Business stabilized at ~$4.5B annualized — permanently repriced from hypergrowth SaaS to mature communications software at ~6x EV/revenue.
why_relevant: The combination of pull-forward normalization and competitive catch-up is a recurring pattern for companies that benefited from pandemic disruption but whose use case was then served by incumbent bundling strategies. The severity (-90%) reflects a double mechanism: the demand reversal AND incumbent displacement (Microsoft Teams bundled with M365). Pure productivity software is particularly vulnerable because switching costs are low.
disanalogy: Remote work permanently increased from pre-COVID baseline — Zoom's revenue floor is higher than a pure demand reversal would suggest. Competitive displacement via Teams requires Microsoft to maintain bundling advantage, which antitrust scrutiny could affect. Pure productivity software has lower switching costs than infrastructure software, making this analog less applicable to enterprise infrastructure vendors.
base_rate_note: Pandemic pull-forward reversals are unique in severity because the demand was borrowed from future years at an extraordinary rate. Normal product adoption reversals are much more gradual. The -90% drawdown reflects both the pull-forward reversal and the realization that the peak run-rate was not achievable even with permanent remote work.

label: Peloton 2021-2022 — fitness hardware pandemic demand reversal
episode: Post-COVID gym reopening demand collapse
outcome_summary: Revenue peaked at $4.0B FY2021, declined to $3.6B FY2022 and continued declining. Peak $171 (January 2021) to trough $6.49 (November 2022), -96%. Management built production capacity and inventory to meet perceived new normal. Gym reopening, inventory glut, and a treadmill recall collided simultaneously. 2,800 layoffs; CEO replaced.
why_relevant: Useful specifically when a business benefited from a behavioral shift (remote work, home fitness, home gaming) that was temporary rather than structural. The lesson is about capital allocation decisions made at peak-demand assumptions — capacity built to the pull-forward run-rate becomes a liability when the demand mean-reverts.
disanalogy: Connected fitness retained some structural behavioral improvement — did not go to zero, only normalized. Pure hardware plays with recurring software revenue have fundamentally worse unit economics when demand reverses than pure software businesses. Peloton's capacity over-building amplified the correction beyond pure demand normalization — a more conservatively managed company would show a different, less severe outcome.
base_rate_note: Consumer hardware companies are particularly vulnerable to pull-forward reversals because they cannot adjust inventory and capacity as quickly as software businesses. The -96% drawdown represents an extreme outcome; most hardware pull-forwards resolve at a meaningfully higher floor.

label: Software/cloud basket 2021-2022 — long-duration equity de-rating
episode: Federal Reserve rate cycle / long-duration SaaS multiple compression
outcome_summary: BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index fell -57%. Median enterprise SaaS company de-rated from ~25x NTM revenue to ~7x NTM revenue. Individual names: Cloudflare -76%, Snowflake -69%, UiPath -87%. Revenue continued growing 30-50%+ throughout the correction. Impairment was purely valuation as 10-year Treasury yields rose from 1.5% to 4.2%.
why_relevant: This is the most precise recent illustration of long-duration equity de-rating. Any company priced above 20x forward revenue in a rising-rate environment is exposed to this mechanism. The speed and uniformity of the 2022 correction (high-quality and low-quality names fell equally) demonstrates that the mechanism punishes the premium itself, not company quality — it is indiscriminate.
disanalogy: Once rates have risen and multiples have compressed, the de-rating mechanism is spent unless rates rise further. AI infrastructure companies earn through cash flow (NVDA margins 75%+) rather than long-duration SaaS contracts — the duration profile is fundamentally different. If rates are declining, the mechanism fully reverses.
base_rate_note: Long-duration equity de-rating occurs in every significant hiking cycle. The 2021-2022 de-rating was particularly severe because starting multiples (20-50x revenue) were at historical extremes; the 1994 and 2000 cycles show similar magnitude compression from comparable starting points.
source_note: BVP Nasdaq Emerging Cloud Index; Bloomberg; individual company 10-K/10-Q filings

label: Amazon 2000-2002 — dot-com peak multiple collapse / survival analog
episode: Dot-com equity bubble deflation
outcome_summary: Peak $113 (December 1999) to trough $5.97 (September 2001), -94%. Amazon bond price at one point implied ~50% bankruptcy probability. Revenue continued growing throughout the correction. Business was not impaired. Stock took 10 years to exceed 1999 peak. Company eventually became worth $2T+.
why_relevant: Invaluable for two distinct questions: (1) how bad can it get if the multiple re-rates from extreme levels, and (2) can the business survive extreme de-rating? Amazon demonstrates that a -94% drawdown is survivable with a durable underlying business model. The survival question is often as important as the downside magnitude question.
disanalogy: Amazon 2000 was burning cash; most 2024 high-multiple tech companies have strong gross margins and FCF. The dot-com collapse was systemic — it took all growth equities with it regardless of quality. Amazon's survival was not guaranteed; most similarly valued companies from 1999 did not survive. Credit market skepticism of internet business models no longer applies to proven platforms.
base_rate_note: The Amazon case demonstrates survivorship bias clearly — it is remembered because it survived. Hundreds of dot-com companies with similar profiles failed. The -94% drawdown required 10 years to recover even for a survivor. The question is not only how far it falls but whether the business survives the de-rating.
source_note: Amazon 10-K 1999-2002; Bloomberg; company bond spreads archived

label: Netflix Q1 2022 — subscriber growth stall / streaming saturation
episode: Streaming market saturation / post-COVID normalization
outcome_summary: First-ever subscriber loss (-200K vs +2.5M expected) in Q1 2022. Peak $700 (November 2021) to trough $162 (May 2022), -77% in six months. Introduced password-sharing crackdown and advertising tier. Recovered above prior peak within 18 months as new monetization vectors re-established growth.
why_relevant: The Netflix case demonstrates that the first miss in a company priced for indefinite growth triggers a binary re-rating. The entire thesis was predicated on growth continuing — when it stopped for one quarter, the market had no intermediate valuation and re-rated to mature comps immediately. The recovery is equally instructive: new growth vectors can re-establish the thesis.
disanalogy: Netflix found new growth vectors (ad tier, password-sharing crackdown). The business was not permanently impaired — it was re-priced and then re-priced again upward. In 2024, Netflix has growing revenue, expanding margins, and diversified monetization. The 2022 analog applies to the growth deceleration setup, not to current financials.
base_rate_note: First misses in hypergrowth companies are disproportionately punished because the entire thesis was predicated on growth continuing. The market has no intermediate valuation — it is either infinite growth or re-rate to mature comps. Recovery is possible if the underlying business model has durable economics.

label: Meta Platforms 2022 — social media growth stall, ATT, competitive pressure
episode: DAU growth stall / Apple ATT signal loss / TikTok competition
outcome_summary: First-ever DAU decline in North America Q4 2021. Revenue declined YoY for first time in Q2 2022. Apple ATT cost estimated $10B in 2022 revenue. Reality Labs losses ~$13B. Peak $382 (September 2021) to trough $88 (November 2022), -77%. Recovered above prior peak by 2023 through cost discipline, Reels monetization, and ad-stack rebuild.
why_relevant: Demonstrates that even a simultaneous multi-mechanism event (growth stall + regulatory break + competitive pressure) does not necessarily imply permanent impairment. Specifically instructive because the business recovered — equally important as a downside illustration is the recovery speed, which depends on execution and platform strength.
disanalogy: Meta rebuilt its ad-measurement stack using on-device modeling and first-party data — the ATT vulnerability is now partially mitigated. Reels proved Meta can compete on short-video format, reducing the competitive displacement thesis. AI investment ($35B+ capex) builds infrastructure for next-generation ad optimization. Meta's 2022 recovery was one of the fastest from a >70% drawdown in large-cap tech history.
base_rate_note: Multi-mechanism adverse events are historically more severe than single-mechanism events, but they also create more recovery catalysts. The Meta case shows that a -77% drawdown from a sound platform business can recover within 18 months if management executes on cost and product adaptation.

label: PayPal 2021-2022 — e-commerce fintech growth deceleration
episode: Post-COVID e-commerce normalization / checkout commoditization
outcome_summary: Management guided to 750M active accounts by 2025; retracted guidance entirely in 2022, admitting ~500M was realistic. Revenue growth stabilized at 8-10%. Peak $310 (July 2021) to trough $62 (January 2023), -80% over 18 months. Multiple has not recovered to prior levels.
why_relevant: Management-issued long-term growth targets that are subsequently withdrawn are often the single most destructive credibility event in hypergrowth deceleration. Once a company has issued and retracted a 3-5 year target, the market treats all future guidance with permanent skepticism — the de-rating discount persists well past the point where the business stabilizes.
disanalogy: PayPal's core payment processing business remains large and profitable — not a failing business, only a repriced one. New leadership abandoned the account-count KPI, removing the specific mechanism that broke credibility. The 2021 fintech premium was narrative-driven; correcting a narrative premium differs from a business impairment.
base_rate_note: Recovery from guidance-retraction credibility events requires multiple clean quarters under new targets and new management — typically 2-3 years before the market normalizes its skepticism discount.

label: Intel 2019-2023 — multi-front architecture competitive displacement
episode: AMD Zen / Apple M1 / ARM datacenter share loss
outcome_summary: Revenue fell from $79B (2021) to $54B (2023), -32%. Gross margins fell from 57% to 40%. AMD Zen 2 (2019) closed IPC gap and attacked desktop/laptop. Apple M1 (2020) removed Intel from entire Apple product line. ARM Graviton gained AWS datacenter share. 7nm delay disclosed 2020 — TSMC pulled ahead in manufacturing.
why_relevant: Intel demonstrates the textbook competitive displacement pattern: attack begins in low-end segments, incumbents dismiss it as limited to price-sensitive buyers, architecture advantage compounds across segments. By the time displacement is acknowledged, it is too late to defend. The gradual pace that causes underestimation is the defining characteristic.
disanalogy: Intel retains unique advantages in legacy x86 software ecosystems with high switching costs. US CHIPS Act provides exogenous manufacturing investment support unavailable to prior displaced incumbents. AI training workloads favor GPU architecture, not CPU market share — Intel's AI displacement dynamic is separate from the AMD CPU story.
base_rate_note: Semiconductor incumbents facing architectural displacement typically decline over 5-10 years, not months. Investors consistently underestimate the endpoint severity at each intermediate stage because the process is gradual. Historical precedents (Motorola CISC vs x86, DEC vs PC servers) did not recover incumbent share.

label: Nokia 2007-2012 — mobile platform disruption by iPhone
episode: Smartphone revolution / iOS platform emergence
outcome_summary: Nokia had 40%+ global mobile market share in 2007 when iPhone launched. Leadership dismissed iPhone as niche (no keyboard, AT&T-only, expensive). iOS App Store created platform lock-in Symbian could not match. By 2012: ~4% smartphone market share. Mobile devices business sold to Microsoft in 2013 for $7.2B.
why_relevant: The Nokia case is the cleanest illustration of platform network effects creating irreversible competitive displacement. Once an ecosystem (App Store, developer community, user behavior) locks in around a new platform, the incumbent's advantages (brand, distribution, manufacturing scale) do not transfer. Specifically applicable to AI: incumbents that do not build the ecosystem layer are vulnerable regardless of capability.
disanalogy: AI models are not yet platform-locked in the way iOS was — switching costs are lower and APIs are more interoperable. Modern tech incumbents can more rapidly acquire or partner. Enterprise market has much higher switching costs than consumer market, making enterprise incumbents significantly more defensible.
base_rate_note: Platform transitions occur faster than incumbent product cycles. Nokia went from 40% share to irrelevance in 5 years. The speed of displacement is the variable most consistently underestimated. Once ecosystem lock-in begins around a new platform, the direction has rarely been reversed historically.
source_note: Nokia annual reports 2007-2013; IDC mobile market share data; Bloomberg

label: Qualcomm 2017-2019 — customer concentration + in-house chip threat (resolved favorably)
episode: Apple modem internalization attempt / FTC antitrust action
outcome_summary: Apple sourced Intel modems to replace Qualcomm starting iPhone 7 (2017) after licensing dispute. Apple was ~15-20% of QCOM revenue. FTC filed antitrust complaint against licensing model. Peak $67 to trough $41, -38% over 15 months. Intel modem program failed. Apple settled with Qualcomm April 2019 and signed multi-year agreement. Stock recovered sharply.
why_relevant: A near-perfect historical test case for the concentration_risk + competitive_displacement combination, with the unique outcome that the displacement threat did NOT materialize. This is the essential negative analog in the library: demonstrates that concentration risk plus internalization threat does not always produce permanent impairment. Any concentration_risk retrieval should consider this case alongside confirmed displacement cases.
disanalogy: Apple did eventually build its own cellular modem (announced 2024) — the threat was delayed, not eliminated. Intel's modem failure was specific to Intel's engineering execution, not a general rule about customer internalization. The QCOM settlement outcome was idiosyncratic; a better-executed internalization attempt would produce a different outcome.
base_rate_note: Customer internalization threats (in-house chip development) are announced more often than they succeed. Technical complexity of wireless silicon is high, and hyperscaler/OEM internal efforts have historically taken 5-10 years to reach commercial quality. However, the threat direction is always maintained over time even when temporarily blocked.

label: Silicon Valley Bank 2023 — deposit base duration mismatch failure
episode: Federal Reserve hiking cycle / VC-backed deposit flight
outcome_summary: SVB had concentrated VC-backed deposits and held long-duration MBS/Treasuries purchased at 2020-2021 low rates, creating $17B in unrealized losses against $16B in equity. Announced capital raise March 8. Sequoia and other VCs advised portfolio companies to withdraw. $42B in withdrawal requests in one day. FDIC seizure March 10, 2023. Largest US bank failure since 2008.
why_relevant: The most precisely documented rate_shock event in recent history. The mechanism — duration mismatch clearly visible on the balance sheet for 18 months before failure — was textbook. Any bank with (a) a concentrated deposit base that may not be sticky and (b) held-to-maturity securities purchased at cycle-low yields is structurally vulnerable to this same mechanism.
disanalogy: Post-SVB regulation requires more frequent stress testing and capital disclosure for mid-size banks — the information asymmetry that allowed SVB to hide unrealized losses for 18 months no longer exists in the same form. The Fed's BTFP created a backstop that was unavailable in 2023. The VC-concentration and social media-accelerated run dynamic was idiosyncratic to SVB's depositor base — traditional commercial banks face a different risk profile.
base_rate_note: Bank runs are self-fulfilling once initiated. The speed (2 days) was a function of SVB's concentrated, tech-savvy depositor base with real-time communication. Traditional commercial banks with diversified retail deposits are structurally slower to run, giving more time for intervention and resolution.
source_note: FDIC SVB failure report 2023; Federal Reserve supervisory review 2023; Bloomberg

label: Annaly Capital / AGNC 2022 — mortgage REIT NAV erosion
episode: Federal Reserve hiking cycle / MBS rate sensitivity
outcome_summary: Mortgage REITs fund MBS portfolios with short-term repo. When rates rose 425bps, cost of funds rose with the short end while MBS assets fell with the long end. Annaly book value fell from $8.77 to $6.50/share (-26%). Dividend cuts followed book value. Total return approximately -40% in 2022.
why_relevant: Useful for any question involving financial intermediaries that hold fixed-rate assets funded with floating-rate liabilities. The mechanism appears whenever liability costs are variable and asset duration is extended to generate yield — a structure that appears across banks, insurance companies, and REITs in various forms.
disanalogy: Mortgage REITs use interest rate swaps that partially offset this mechanism; 2022 severity was amplified because hedges were imperfect and the rate rise was faster than swap coverage. In a rate-easing environment, the mechanism fully reverses. Agency MBS carries government backing limiting credit loss — pure interest rate risk, not credit risk.
base_rate_note: Mortgage REIT returns are highly correlated with the shape of the yield curve. Rate-easing cycles produce near-total recoveries in agency mortgage REITs because there is no credit impairment — only duration mismatch, which unwinds as the rate environment normalizes.

label: Washington Mutual 2008 — CRE/mortgage loan portfolio failure
episode: US housing crisis / subprime mortgage defaults
outcome_summary: WaMu aggressively grew Option ARM and subprime mortgage book 2004-2007 in California/Florida/Nevada, requiring permanently rising home prices to avoid default. Loans began defaulting 2007. Bank run after IndyMac FDIC seizure July 2008. FDIC seizure September 25, 2008 — largest US bank failure at the time ($307B assets). Acquired by JPMorgan for $1.9B.
why_relevant: The canonical credit_event + cre_credit_risk case. Directly relevant when a bank has high CRE or residential mortgage exposure in markets experiencing price stress. The mechanism — asset quality deteriorates slowly then all at once, confidence withdraws, FDIC acts — is directly applicable to any bank with concentrated real estate loan exposure.
disanalogy: Post-GFC Dodd-Frank regulation created much higher capital requirements — a WaMu-equivalent would be caught by stress tests years earlier. Option ARMs no longer exist as a loan product. Most 2024 bank CRE stress is in commercial office with longer loan maturities and less consumer concentration — transmission is slower than residential mortgage 2007-2008.
base_rate_note: Retail bank failures via credit event require both asset quality deterioration AND confidence withdrawal. Capital adequacy requirements under Basel III mean confidence withdrawal is much harder to trigger — the pre-GFC 8% capital ratios that made WaMu vulnerable no longer apply to well-capitalized banks.
source_note: FDIC WaMu failure report; Federal Reserve GFC analysis; Bloomberg

label: Bear Stearns 2007-2008 — leveraged balance sheet confidence collapse
episode: GFC / mortgage-backed securities crisis
outcome_summary: Bear Stearns operated at 35:1 leverage. Two internal MBS hedge funds failed June 2007. Counterparties withdrew repo financing. When repo funding evaporated, the firm could not maintain liquidity. Acquired by JPMorgan at $2/share (from $170 peak, -99%) in March 2008 via Fed-facilitated transaction.
why_relevant: Illustrates the systemic credit event mechanism: highly interconnected leveraged institutions can fail in days when counterparty confidence withdraws. The speed is qualitatively different from operational mechanisms. Useful specifically for questions about systemic financial risk or contagion scenarios where counterparty confidence is the key variable.
disanalogy: Dodd-Frank OTC derivatives reform (central clearing, margin requirements) removed the opacity that made Bear's MBS exposure invisible to counterparties. Investment banks no longer operate as standalone dealers outside commercial bank holding structures. Fed emergency lending facilities are now broader and faster to activate than in 2008.
base_rate_note: Systemic credit events require both the mechanism (leverage + opacity) and the environment (no backstop, no clearing). The post-GFC regulatory environment has explicitly addressed both variables. The Bear Stearns analog applies to the setup (leverage + opaque assets + counterparty confidence); the speed and severity are specific to the pre-Dodd-Frank environment.
source_note: SEC/Fed emergency authority documentation; Bear Stearns bankruptcy filings; Bloomberg

label: Alibaba 2020-2022 — Chinese tech regulatory crackdown
episode: China SAMR antitrust action / PBOC Ant Group fintech restrictions
outcome_summary: Ant Group $37B IPO suspended days before listing (November 2020). Alibaba fined $2.8B for antitrust violations 2021. VIE structure legal validity publicly questioned. DiDi's NYSE listing triggered sector-wide concerns about US-listed Chinese ADRs. Peak $306 (October 2020) to trough $59 (October 2022), -81%. Revenue continued growing; impairment was entirely valuation/risk-premium.
why_relevant: The strongest modern example of a single regulatory intervention changing the risk/reward profile of an entire sector permanently. Any company with VIE exposure, ADR listing, or significant revenue from a jurisdiction with a history of private capital restriction deserves this analog. The VIE structure risk, which existed from the beginning, became priced in only when the government chose to highlight it.
disanalogy: Chinese government shifted back toward supporting private tech (2023 leadership discussions, Ant Group restructuring progressing). The specific trigger (Jack Ma's speech) was idiosyncratic — a political event as much as regulatory. VIE structure risk is now priced in by every analyst — the same structural vulnerability that surprised in 2020 is no longer a surprise. A surprise cannot repeat when it is already in every model.
base_rate_note: Regulatory risk in jurisdictions with concentrated government authority is binary: once the government decides to tolerate or support a sector, the discount reverses. The Chinese tech sector has traded between these poles multiple times. The risk premium itself is the key variable, not the fundamental revenue trajectory.
source_note: SAMR Alibaba fine announcement 2021; PBOC Ant Group restructuring; Bloomberg

label: Meta 2021 — Apple ATT privacy disruption signal loss
episode: iOS 14.5 App Tracking Transparency rollout
outcome_summary: Apple iOS 14.5 (April 2021) required explicit IDFA opt-in; opt-in rates ~25%. Meta lost estimated $10B in 2022 revenue vs pre-ATT run-rate. Revenue declined for first time Q2 2022. Operating income fell 46% YoY. Ad measurement, targeting, and attribution systems built on IDFA were impaired for 18+ months.
why_relevant: The cleanest modern example of a platform rule change by a third-party gatekeeper structurally impairing a dependent business's revenue model. Any advertising-dependent business with significant iOS traffic is exposed to equivalent risk if Apple further tightens privacy controls or Google enacts comparable Privacy Sandbox changes.
disanalogy: Meta substantially rebuilt its measurement stack using on-device processing (Conversions API, Privacy-Enhancing Technologies) — the ATT vulnerability is now partially mitigated. EU DMA may reduce Apple's ability to impose similar restrictions in Europe. The $10B revenue loss proved manageable — advertisers did not reduce budgets, they adapted measurement approaches.
base_rate_note: Platform rule changes by third-party gatekeepers are a recurring risk for ad-supported businesses. Privacy changes typically create temporary measurement disruption rather than permanent ad spend loss — advertisers adapt measurement approaches rather than stopping spending. The base case is adaptation, not permanent revenue loss.

label: Oil supermajors 2014-2016 — OPEC supply defense price collapse
episode: US shale supply surge / OPEC market share defense
outcome_summary: US shale rose from 5mbd (2010) to 9.6mbd (2014). OPEC chose not to offset with production cuts. Brent fell from $115/bbl to $28/bbl, -76%. XOM fell ~35% peak to trough; COP fell ~65%; exploration-focused E&Ps fell 70-90%. Integrated majors survived via downstream refining/chemicals profitability. Recovery took 2-3 years as demand absorbed supply.
why_relevant: Illustrates how an external price event can impair an operationally sound business. The critical lesson is business model diversification as the survivorship variable: integrated majors survived via downstream offsetting upstream losses; pure E&Ps did not. The mechanism is directly applicable to any commodity-exposed business where input or output prices are outside management control.
disanalogy: US shale has matured and marginal cost of supply increase is higher than 2014 because best rock has been drilled. OPEC+ (including Russia) has demonstrated more flexibility in response. Long-term energy transition risk adds a secular demand floor question that changes the risk/reward calculus permanently — oil demand may peak mid-2020s, which was not a factor in 2014.
base_rate_note: Commodity shocks in integrated energy companies are survivable through business model diversification (upstream + downstream + chemicals). Pure exploration companies are not. The key variable in outcome severity is business model diversification, not asset quality or reserve life.
source_note: EIA production data; Brent crude price history; XOM/CVX/COP 10-K filings 2014-2017
